node.label: Charles E. Rosenberg
node.description: A historian of medicine and science. The Cholera Years (1962), on the United States in 1832, 1849 and 1866, is credited with leading historians to study not only a disease and its victims but society’s response to it, through politics, law and social mores. The Care of Strangers (1987), a history of the American hospital, and Explaining Epidemics (1992) continued that social history of medicine. In a 2013 interview he places his work within a social-medicine tradition that treats medical ideas and access to care as embedded in society, questions tidy genealogies in which translated theorists alone changed historical research, and distinguishes psychiatric diagnostic categories that organize research and care from explanations of mechanism.
